claude.performance_metric: no divestiture; assets retained (targeted ~$250m cost savings in 2019)
claude.rationale: Section 2 shows T4 (the ~250,000 homesites / ~1,300 communities) and T5 (operations slated for integration to capture cost savings and production efficiencies) transferred together as a whole-entity statutory merger, so no product-vs-process mismatch at closing (gap_45=0); people also transferred with partial senior-leadership retention alongside the operations, so no process-vs-organization mismatch (gap_56=0). Section 4 documents no P4 product-process disruption (inventory and processes integrated together) and no P5 process-organization fracture (marked [UNVERIFIED]/none documented), so both pathways coded 0. Section 4 also records aligned intent and compatible business models, supporting t1_archetype=0 and t2_model=0.

gemini.performance_metric: No divestiture identified; targeted direct cost savings of $75m in 2018 and $250m in 2019
gemini.rationale: The dossier documents a whole-entity statutory merger where CalAtlantic's product (homesites/communities), processes (operations), and organization (people/leadership) transferred together to Lennar without structural gaps at closing (gap_45=0, gap_56=0). Post-deal, there is no documented disruption at the product-process interface (p4_pathway=0) or the process-organization interface (p5_pathway=0).

grok.rationale: T4 transferred whole (section 2: ~250k homesites/1300 communities) while T5 was slated only for integration (section 2), but no structural mismatch at closing is documented, yielding gap_45=0. T5 and T6 both coded partial with leadership retention noted (section 2), and no process-org fracture documented at 3-5yr horizon (section 4), yielding gap_56=0, p4_pathway=0 and p5_pathway=0. T1 replaced (section 2) with no archetype incoherence or model incompatibility documented (section 4).
